statusMeaning.supported: a generated app boots, serves and persists on this engine, proven in CI
statusMeaning.experimental: the dialect is complete and passes conformance against a real engine, but no generated application has been proven end to end on it. Usable; not yet something to rely on.

engines.summary: File-backed H2 in the app's own process. No server to install. The default. Commits schema changes implicitly: a failed schema change is not fully rolled back -- see `npdev capabilities`.

H2 in TCP server mode, so more than one process can share the database. Nothing to install: the H2 jar ships with every generated app and its _ops/Start-Environment starts the server. Also commits schema changes implicitly -- see `npdev capabilities`.
PostgreSQL 16. The engine NPDev's schema engine was built against. The app's _ops/Start-Environment runs it in Docker for you, or point the app at a server you already run.

MySQL 8.4+. The app's _ops/Start-Environment runs it in Docker for you (already utf8mb4), or point the app at a server you already run -- which must use utf8mb4: the legacy three-byte 'utf8' cannot store emoji or other characters outside the BMP (`npdev doctor` checks this).
engines.caveat: MySQL COMMITS IMPLICITLY ON DDL, so a migration that fails partway CANNOT be rolled back: earlier steps are already permanent. NPDev reports this truthfully (PartialApplicationTruth) rather than claiming a rollback, but it is a real operational difference from Postgres.

engines.summary: Microsoft SQL Server 2022+. The app's _ops/Start-Environment runs it in Docker for you, or point the app at a server you already run.
engines.caveat: Text columns are mapped to NVARCHAR so unicode survives -- plain VARCHAR is non-Unicode there and loses characters silently.

engines.summary: Nothing is persisted. Everything is lost when the app stops -- tests and demos only.
